title: Higher direct-image exchange tested on strict-local cohomology
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ and $g:T\to S$ be morphisms of schemes [def-pc-scheme], with $g$ quasi-compact [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] and quasi-separated [def-weil-quasi-separated-morphism]. Form $Y=X\times_S T$ [def-pc-fibre-product], with projections $h:Y\to X$ and $e:Y\to T$. Let $F$ be an abelian etale sheaf on $T$ [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves] and let $q\geq0$. The canonical exchange $f^{-1}R^qg_*F\to R^qh_*e^{-1}F$ [sbc-def-base-change-map], using inverse image [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image] and higher direct image [def-weil-pbc-direct-image], is an isomorphism if and only if, for every geometric point $\bar x$ of $X$ with $\bar s=f\bar x$ [def-weil-geometric-point], the canonical pullback map [def-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback] $$H^q(S_{(\bar s)}\times_S T,F)\longrightarrow H^q(X_{(\bar x)}\times_S T,F)$$ is an isomorphism. Here the strict henselizations are those of [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit], their map is the canonical one of [lem-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-functoriality], and cohomology [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology] uses the inverse image of $F$ under the projections to $T$.
